# Indikator 7a

Indikator 7a is one of the quality indicators tracked in Denmark's ADHD database, measuring the share of young people in the "ADHD-udredningspopulation" (ADHD assessment population) who have passed the final exam of the Danish primary/lower-secondary school (folkeskolens afgangseksamen) before turning 17 [^src1]. It functions as a proxy for educational attainment among youth who have gone through ADHD diagnostic assessment, forming part of a broader set of 11 quality indicators presented in the ADHD database's annual report covering the period 1 April 2024 to 31 March 2025 [^src1].

According to the data, fulfillment of Indikator 7a was 53% (confidence interval 51–55%) for the period 01.04.2024–31.03.2025, down from 57% in 2023/24 and 59% in 2022/23 [^src1]. This declining trend places the indicator, like most others tracked in the same report, well below the stated development target of ≥90% [^src1]. The broader annual report describes ongoing work to revise and improve the indicator set so that it better reflects clinical practice in ADHD diagnosis and treatment across the Danish healthcare system, and the report also introduces new indicators for adult ADHD patients [^src1] — context that situates Indikator 7a as part of a wider effort to measure and improve outcomes for people undergoing ADHD assessment and treatment in Denmark.

No relationships to other named entities are recorded for Indikator 7a in the available data.
